newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mandela to pay official visit to Britain.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela to pay official visit to Britain.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela and his companion, Graca Machel of Mozambique, will meet Queen Elizabeth and Prime Minister Tony Blair during an official visit to Britain next week, the Foreign Ministry said on Tuesday.
A ministry statement said Mandela and Machel, widow of former Mozambican president Samora Machel, would be in Britain from July 8 to 12.
South African officials said recently Mandela would be making a private visit to London, but Tuesday's statement said it would be "of an official nature".

Taking advantage of the government's mid-winter recess, Mandela, who turns 79 on July 18, will accompany Machel to a University of Essex graduation ceremony where she will receive an honorary degree on July 10.
She will accompany him to Oxford, where he will receive the freedom of the city on July 11, deliver a lecture to the Centre for Islamic Studies and attend a dinner with Prince Charles.
Machel is an international ambassador for children's rights, and has worked for the U.N. on a study of war and its effect on children.
The couple spend about two weeks a month together and she has accompanied Mandela on most of his recent travels.
Mandela is expected to travel on to Thailand and Indonesia.
The Foreign Ministry said he would return to Britain in October for the Commonwealth heads of government meeting in Edinburgh.
